points.description: States that height is a length/measure of a path starting at the root (path from the root downward). Accept equivalent wording such as 'distance from the root'.

levels.says: Mentions a path or distance but does not clearly start from the root, or is vague about the start.

points.description: States that the path ends at a leaf (a node with no children), i.e. goes from the root to a leaf/deepest node. Accept 'deepest node' or 'farthest node'.

levels.says: Refers to going down to the bottom or to any node without specifying a leaf/deepest node.

points.description: States that it is the longest (maximum) such path, i.e. the maximum over all root-to-leaf paths. A shortest, average or arbitrary path does not earn this mark.

Measures the length as the number of edges (or, if clearly stated, nodes) on that path. Accept either convention if stated explicitly; unspecified units are acceptable if the definition is otherwise correct.

rubric.notes: Full marks for: the length of the longest path from the root to a leaf (any equivalent wording, e.g. maximum depth of any leaf). Part marks for partially correct definitions, e.g. 'distance from the root to a leaf' without 'longest' earns P1 and P2 only. Confusing height with number of nodes or with shortest path earns no mark for the affected point.
